subject: Post-call: MidCity Bank eval setup + dataset/metrics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@midcitybank.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@midcitybank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: MidCity Bank eval setup + dataset/metrics

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great to meet with you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the MidCity evaluation running on Redwood: 

1) Goal: run a customer-specific evaluation for your transaction categorization and fraud triage prompts (10k examples; mix of single-label and multi-label cases) to compare model fit and check for any quality regressions against your current baseline.

2) Recommended models to include in the benchmark: 
   - redwood/13B-opt (quantized) — strong cost/latency tradeoff for high-throughput routing
   - redwood/13B-retry (higher quality, slightly higher cost)
   - open/llama-2-70b-instruct (as a higher-capacity reference)
   - a low-cost distilled baseline (for production baseline comparisons)

3) Dataset/format: We prefer JSONL with fields: id, prompt, reference (label or gold response), metadata (customer_id/payload_type). See attached redwood_eval_template.jsonl and the Drive folder link. CSV samples are fine for initial upload but we ask that the evaluation dataset be normalized to JSONL before we run batch scoring.

4) Scoring criteria & thresholds: Exact match for single-label tasks (EM), macro-F1 for multi-label classification, and a human-eval spot-check for open-ended responses. We typically flag regressions when a model drops >3 points absolute in macro-F1 versus your baseline or fails >5% of high-severity examples.

5) Logistics & next steps:
   - Samantha: please share the sanitized dataset (S3 link or Drive) and a short description of which fields are PII/sensitive.
   - Neha: will confirm the evaluation pipeline (format, sampling, metrics) and share estimated run time/cost.
   - Connor: will scope any additional infra needs for streaming or large-batch runs.

Attached: redwood_eval_template.jsonl (schema + small sample), midcity_eval_dataset_sample.csv (10 rows).

If that all sounds right, can we lock a kickoff window next Tuesday morning PST to finalize the pipeline and get the dataset uploaded?

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0162
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@midcitybank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@midcitybank.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: MidCity Bank eval setup + dataset/metrics

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. Quick updates: 

- I've uploaded the sanitized sample and full dataset to our S3 bucket (link in Drive folder): s3://midcity-data/redwood-evals/2027-02-25/. The files include a README that flags which columns are PII and which can be used verbatim.
- Primary task: transaction categorization (single-label, ~8k examples) + fraud triage (multi-label, ~2k examples with severity tags).
- Baseline: our current in-house classifier (macro-F1 = 82.5 on the holdout) — we'll expect the first pass to be compared against that.

We can do the kickoff Tuesday 02 Mar, 10:00 AM PST. Please send a calendar invite.

Also: one ask — can Redwood include model-specific prompt templates and the exact prompt sets you plan to run so our security team can pre-review content flows?

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee | Head of Data Science, MidCity Bank
samantha.lee@midcitybank.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@midcitybank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 07:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: MidCity Bank eval setup + dataset/metrics

Hi Samantha — thanks, this is perfect. A few technical clarifications from the evaluation engineering side: 

- Required JSONL schema: {id, prompt, reference, type, severity(optional), metadata}. We attached redwood_eval_template.jsonl for exact field names. Please ensure multi-label references are pipe-delimited (e.g., "labelA|labelC") or provide a mapping file.
- Label mapping: include a labels.csv if your label set isn't self-explanatory.
- Sampling & scoring: we'll run an initial smoke run on a 1,000-sample stratified subset (preserving class distribution + severity buckets) to validate prompts and metrics. Then we'll run the full batch. Expected turn-around: smoke run within 24 hours of dataset ingestion; full run typically 6-12 hours depending on model mix.
- Metrics we will compute: Accuracy / Exact Match (single-label), Macro-F1 (multi-label), per-label precision/recall, latency p50/p95, and a small human-eval sample for open-ended triage explanations. We'll generate a regression report that highlights deltas vs your baseline and flags examples with high severity where model confidence is low.
- Quality regression guardrails: we recommend setting an alert if Macro-F1 drops by >3 points OR if the rate of high-severity false negatives increases by >2%. We'll include confusion matrices and per-severity breakdowns in the report.

Prompt sets & templates: we'll share the exact prompt templates ahead of the smoke run (sensitive content redactions applied per your guidance). Marissa — can you confirm the owner for prompt review on your side? Samantha — please confirm if security needs to sign an NDA or if the redacted prompt templates are fine as-is.

I'll attach the evaluation template we run internally (redwood_eval_template.jsonl) and a short runbook.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor | Eval Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@redwoodbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: MidCity Bank eval setup + dataset/metrics

Thanks everyone — all good from my side. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- Samantha: confirmed kickoff Tue 2027-03-02 10:00 AM PST (I'll send the invite momentarily).
- Action items before kickoff:
   * Samantha: add the full sanitized dataset to the Drive or S3 path and confirm label mapping file (by Mon EOD).
   * Security: please indicate whether an NDA is required for the redacted prompt templates — otherwise we'll share templates ahead of the smoke run.
   * Neha / Connor: please prepare the smoke run config (models to include, sampling seed, and evaluation budget estimate).

Expected deliverables after the run: a regression dashboard (macro-F1 deltas, per-label breakdown), sample failure analysis with recommended prompt/template adjustments, and cost/latency estimates per model to help you choose production routing policy.

HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876 — I've tagged the kickoff and set the next milestone to "smoke run complete."

Looking forward to it —
Marissa
